 Michaelmas 2026 Read the issue November 16, 2026 7:00 AM Austrian priest calls for Church to reconsider its relationship with Freemasonry
 Mgr Michael Heinrich Weninger has argued that Freemasonry should not be treated as uniformly hostile to Catholicism, despite the Vatican’s reaffirmation in 2023 that Catholics may not become Freemasons
 Corrie Douglas-Young English Español Getty Images Corrie Douglas-Young More Europe Catholic Church Related The Catholic Herald The Week Ahead: Red Wednesday, US bishops’ meeting and more Nathalie Raffray Syrian nun who stayed in Aleppo during civil war to receive ACN award The Catholic Herald Belfast City Hall to be illuminated for abortion campaign on Easter Sunday 3 min read share An Austrian priest and former diplomat has called for a re-examination of the relationship between Freemasonry and Catholicism. Speaking at a conference in Lübeck, Mgr Michael Heinrich Weninger stated that a Freemason was “basically a good person who works on himself to become an even better one”.
 Fr Weninger said that, as a Catholic priest, he could not “fault that for the time being”. He stated that there was no “copyright” on the label and that “any lunatic can call himself a Freemason”, the Austrian publication Aussicht reported.
